newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on soybean drop, crop ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on soybean drop, crop ideas.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a drop in soybeans coupled with ideas USDA's November crop production report, slated for release November 12, will show an increase in U.S. corn production, traders said.
Pressure also came from a continued bearish technical picture plus only routine export business, they said.
Corn was underpinned by slow farmer selling plus some talk that harsh weather in the U.S. Midwest may have harmed some of the crop that hasn't been harvested.
Traders said commercial bear spreading indicated further declines in the market were possible.
Continental Grain spread three million May/March and did three million July/May plus two million bushels of July/March and two million July/December, traders said.

Corn also was said pressured Tuesday by apparent confusion about an IRS memo that may have indicated farmers will store rather than sell their crops. Apparently the IRS memo should not have affected the market, industry sources said.
Technical traders cited resistance in the December at $2.76 a bushel and support at $272-1/2 with second support at $2.69.
Corn closed 4-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 3-1/2 higher, with December down 4-1/4 at $2.70-1/4.
The session high for December was $2.75 and the session low was $2.70.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 18.5 points. The market generally considers an RSI of 30 or less as an oversold market.
Chart watchers said the key moving averages show corn remains in a bearish mode.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 58,000 contracts, down from 65,889 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Refco Inc bought 500 December $3.00 calls at 3/8 cent and sold 500 March $2.90 calls at 7-1/2 cents, traders said. Tradelink bought 400 December $2.90 puts and sold 400 December $2.70 puts at 14-3/4 to 15 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 23,000 contracts, down from 30,114 Tuesday.
